en: Dr. Fe del Mundo designed an improvised bamboo incubator to provide affordable medical care for newborn babies in rural Philippine areas.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically known as Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
General Emilio Aguinaldo officially proclaimed Philippine independence from Spanish colonial rule on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The legislative branch of the Philippine government is called Congress, which is divided into the Senate with twenty-four members and the House of Representatives.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao province are ancient agricultural structures carved into the mountains by indigenous ancestors over two thousand years ago.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu City honors the Santo Niño through a vibrant street dance featuring a distinctive two-steps-forward, one-step-backward rhythm.
The Lumad is a collective term for various indigenous groups in Mindanao who practice their own distinct traditional beliefs and agricultural customs.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system that uses specific symbols to represent vowels and consonants, often carved on bamboo or leaves.
Juan Luna painted the famous masterpiece Spoliarium, which won a gold medal at the National Exhibition of Fine Arts in Madrid in 1884.
Under the Philippine Constitution, every citizen who is at least eighteen years old and meets the residency requirements has the right to vote.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine flower, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Bayanihan is a traditional Filipino cultural value where community members work together to help a family physically relocate their traditional nipa hut.
